title: Nonthaburi Attractions 2026 — 12 Best Things to Do | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: The best things to do in Nonthaburi, Thailand: car-free Koh Kret and its Mon community, riverside temples, the old town at Tha Nam Non, green riverside parks and floating markets. An easy day trip right next to Bangkok.
keywords: Nonthaburi attractions, Koh Kret, Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat, Tha Nam Non, Nonthaburi park
intro: Nonthaburi sits right next to Bangkok, just across the river, yet plenty of corners still hold onto that old Chao Phraya riverside feel: a car-free island in the middle of the water, a riverside temple full of Chinese-influenced art, the old town around Tha Nam Non, and green parks made for an easy stroll. We've picked 12 spots that mix culture, city life and nature, enough to fill anything from a half day to two days.

blocks.html: The nice thing about Nonthaburi is how close it is. Hop on the MRT Purple Line or take a Chao Phraya express boat and you're there, which makes it perfect for Bangkok folks who want to slip out for the day without a long drive. What the province does best is its riverside way of life: a Mon community that still throws clay pottery by hand, and old temples with real artwork worth a look. We've split the attractions into three groups so it's easy to put a trip together.

blocks.text: Culture — Koh Kret, the Mon community and old temples

blocks.html: If you only have one day, this is the group you can't skip. Koh Kret and the temples around it are really the heart of Nonthaburi, pulling food, crafts and history together in one place.

items.name: Koh Kret
items.blurb: An island in the middle of the Chao Phraya with not a single car on it, so you can walk or cycle the whole loop. The Mon community here has lived on the island for more than 400 years, still throwing clay pottery by hand and selling hard-to-find Thai sweets. It's busiest on Saturdays and Sundays, with far more shops open than on weekdays.
items.meta: Open daily, best Sat–Sun · cross-river ferry from Wat Sanam Nuea THB 2–4

items.name: Wat Poramai Yikawat (Koh Kret)
items.blurb: An old Mon temple on Koh Kret, once known as Wat Pak Ao. Its leaning Mon-style riverside chedi is the island's landmark. Inside there's a small museum holding antiques and palm-leaf scriptures. It makes an easy first stop the moment your ferry lands on the island.
items.meta: On Koh Kret, next to the pier · free entry

items.name: Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat Worawihan
items.blurb: A Chao Phraya riverside temple built in the reign of Rama III that blends Chinese art with Thai craftsmanship beautifully. There's a large bronze Buddha image in the ordination hall, and since it doesn't get crowded the mood stays calm, a good spot to rest and look out over the river.
items.meta: Mueang Nonthaburi district · open 05:30–18:30 · free entry

items.name: Nonthaburi Provincial Museum (old city hall)
items.blurb: An old wooden building from 1910 that once served as the provincial city hall, now a museum telling the story of Nonthaburi. The upper floor displays the locally famous pottery. It's only 160 m from Tha Nam Non, so you can easily walk over.

items.name: Wat Bua Khwan (royal temple)
items.blurb: An old temple dating to the reign of Rama V, in the city centre of Nonthaburi. Locals come here to make merit regularly. It has an ordination hall and a shady, peaceful feel, worth a stop if you want a temple on the town side that's easy to reach by car.

blocks.title: Which day to visit Koh Kret
blocks.html: The shops and market on Koh Kret are only fully open on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. Go on a weekday and it's quiet, with a lot of shops shut. Aim to arrive a bit early, around 10–11 am, while it's still uncrowded and the sun isn't too harsh.

items.label: Day trips from Nonthaburi
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: City — riverside, markets and local life

blocks.html: The Nonthaburi town side is fun to wander, especially the Tha Nam Non area where food, market and ferry pier all sit together. It suits anyone who likes an old riverside town that's still very much alive.

items.name: Tha Nam Non (old town market)
items.blurb: A riverside district that's part market, part Chao Phraya express boat pier and the starting point for a walk through the old town. Tasty food stalls line up one after another, so you can graze your way along the river for ages. Easy to reach by boat or the MRT Purple Line.

items.name: Wat Takhian floating market
items.blurb: A small canalside floating market selling Thai sweets and home-style local food. A relaxed place to stroll and snack, and nowhere near as crowded as the famous floating markets.

items.name: Sai Noi floating market
items.blurb: A floating market out in Sai Noi district, focused on home-style local food and an old-fashioned canalside garden setting. Good if you want to get a little further from the city.

blocks.title: The easiest way to get around
blocks.html: The town side and Tha Nam Non are reachable on the MRT Purple Line (several stations across Nonthaburi), then a short hop by boat or motorcycle taxi. For Koh Kret, the easiest route is to drive or take a taxi to Wat Sanam Nuea in Pak Kret, then catch the cross-river ferry for a few baht.

blocks.text: Nature — green parks and the riverside

blocks.html: If you want an open spot to unwind, Nonthaburi has riverside parks along the Chao Phraya for walking, running or cycling, good for bringing the family or just sitting and chilling in the evening.

items.name: Somdet Phra Srinagarindra Park, Nonthaburi
items.blurb: A riverside park on the Chao Phraya in the city centre, with a botanical garden, a lake, a Thai pavilion and shady paths. It's near Tha Nam Non, ideal for an evening walk catching the river breeze or letting the kids run around.
items.meta: Near Tha Nam Non, Mueang district · free entry

items.name: Cycling around Koh Kret
items.blurb: The loop around Koh Kret is flat and car-free, so you can ride past gardens, wooden houses and Mon temples the whole way around. There are bike rental shops near the pier, and it's a better way to see the island than walking alone.
items.meta: Bike rental on the island THB 20–40/day

items.name: A river cruise along the Chao Phraya
items.blurb: Take an express boat or cross-river ferry to take in the views on both banks: temples, riverside houses and the life of the boat people. It's a side of Nonthaburi you'd never see from the road, and the ticket is only a few baht.
items.meta: Chao Phraya express boat · from a few baht

blocks.html: With half a day, just focusing on Koh Kret is plenty: wander the market, pay respects at Wat Poramai Yikawat and try the Mon sweets. With a full day, add the town side, Tha Nam Non, the museum and Somdet Phra Srinagarindra Park in the evening. If you want to round out the temples, add Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat too, so you mix culture, city and nature in one day.

items: Half day — Koh Kret: take the cross-river ferry, pay respects at Wat Poramai Yikawat, wander the market, try the Mon sweets and cycle around the island
Full day — morning on Koh Kret · afternoon over to the town side, Tha Nam Non and the provincial museum · evening stroll in Somdet Phra Srinagarindra Park by the river
Temple route — Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat (riverside Chinese art) + Wat Poramai Yikawat (Mon chedi) + Wat Bua Khwan in town

faq.q: What are the must-see attractions in Nonthaburi?
faq.a: Koh Kret is the one most people think of first, with its Mon community, pottery and hard-to-find Thai sweets. After that come Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat with its riverside Chinese art, the old town at Tha Nam Non, and Somdet Phra Srinagarindra Park for anyone after a bit of nature.

faq.q: Which day should I visit Koh Kret, and is it open every day?
faq.a: Koh Kret is open every day, but the shops and market are only fully open on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. Go on a weekday and it's quiet with many shops shut, so it's best to visit on a weekend, mid-morning.

faq.q: How many days do I need for Nonthaburi?
faq.a: Half a day is enough for Koh Kret on its own. If you also want to cover the town side, Tha Nam Non, the museum and the riverside park, allow a full day. It works easily as a day trip from Bangkok.

faq.q: How do I get to Nonthaburi?
faq.a: The town side and Tha Nam Non are reachable by the MRT Purple Line and the Chao Phraya express boat. For Koh Kret, the easiest way is to drive or take a taxi to Pak Kret / Wat Sanam Nuea, then catch the cross-river ferry for a few baht.

Yes. Koh Kret is safe to walk and cycle since there are no cars, Somdet Phra Srinagarindra Park has space for kids to run around by the river, there's plenty of food, and you can take the grandparents along to visit the temples.
